overview: Rise 5.99's Jesus walks on water through a client-side collision override plus C03 y-offsets. The Solid and NCP modes replace the collision bounding box of every BlockLiquid with a full block via onBlockCollide, so the player stands on the water surface locally and never sinks; the Boost and Jump modes skip the override and instead pump motionY while spoofing the onGround flag. Every mode drives an ascensionValue of 0.06000000238418583 while in liquid or while jumping on liquid, a constant the source labels the fastest legit water ascension value, and the NCP mode adds a periodic event y shift of minus 0.015625 every second tick while standing on liquid: that offset sits below the 0.03 minimum move the server applies, so each shifted C03 leaves the coordinate untouched while the slow descent keeps the server-side position creeping into the water column.

sections.p: onBlockCollide fires for every block collision the client computes, and the Solid and NCP modes replace the liquid AABB with a full 1x1x1 box, but only when the player is not in liquid and is not sneaking or jumping. The override makes the client's own physics treat water as solid, so the player walks across at constant Y without sinking, and it is purely client-side: the server never learns about the replaced box. Boost and Jump do not override the box and rely entirely on motion to stay above the surface.

Boost and Jump both set motionY to the motion setting (default 0.2) and the onGround flag to true while standing on liquid, and Boost additionally calls MoveUtil.strafe with the speed setting (default 1.0, up to 9.5), which rewrites the horizontal motion vector toward the movement input at that speed. The onGround true claim over water is a ground spoof: vanilla ground state follows the collision box, and the module fakes the flag so the server sees a grounded player standing on a surface that is not solid.

The NCP mode sets the event's y coordinate to minus 0.015625 every second tick while standing on liquid and the Speed module is off. One sixty-fourth of a block is below the 0.03 minimum move, so each shifted C03 leaves the server-side coordinate effectively unchanged while the onGround flag on the packet still applies; the slowly descending series keeps the server-side position just under the surface line, which is the classic water-column trick that makes the player read as in-water without any visible jump. The NCP mode also enables the full-block collision override like Solid, and every mode returns early when the sneak key is held.

files.label: Jesus.java
files.explanation: onPreMotion runs the mode switch: the ascensionValue constant drives motionY in liquid, the Boost and Jump branches write motion and the onGround flag when PlayerUtil.isOnLiquid holds, and the NCP branch shifts the event y by minus 0.015625 every second tick. onBlockCollide installs the full-block override for Solid and NCP, and the sneak and jump key guards gate both handlers. The motion and speed settings only surface in the Boost and Jump branches, which the GUI visibility logic reflects.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (liquid ground detector)
files.explanation: isOnLiquid is the ground detector the module leans on: it offsets the player bounding box down 0.01, walks every column cell the box covers at the resulting y, and returns true only when every block there is liquid and none is solid. All four modes branch on it to decide when to apply motion, and the NCP mode gates its periodic y-shift on it, so the module's entire surface-detection behavior is defined by this scan.

countering.label: Flight (Jesus)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Flight check, inside the ascending or descending branch, tests the destination with LocationHelper.isInLiquid and compares the client-claimed onGround flag against the server-computed ground state: when the client claims onGround while in liquid and the vertical speed is positive, the check names itself Flight (Jesus) and flags walking on water with the ccground_liquid reason. That lands directly on the Boost and Jump modes, which set onGround true and motionY 0.2 on liquid, and on the 0.06 ascension in any mode when the player's feet sit in the column while rising.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (liquid envelope)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus SurvivalFly switches to the liquid physics model when the server-side position is in water: the horizontal allowance comes from estimateNextSpeed with WATER_HORIZONTAL_INERTIA and LIQUID_ACCELERATION, and the vertical side applies the 0.02 legacy liquid gravity for 1.8 clients. A player inside the water column moving at air speed exceeds the liquid horizontal allowance, and the Boost mode's strafe at 1.0 to 9.5 overshoots it by an order of magnitude, so any time the boosted player's feet dip into the column the envelope flags and set-backs. The Solid and NCP modes aim to keep the server-side position above the water line so the liquid branch never engages, which is their bypass surface; the honest counter is that the envelope still owns the column the moment the override drifts in.

countering.label: SwimVertical (liquid vertical physics)
countering.explanation: Hawk SwimVertical models the in-liquid vertical physics: while the server-side player is swimming and not really on ground, the move delta Y must fall inside kinetic preservation times the previous velocity plus or minus MOVE_LIQUID_FORCE (0.02) and the water flow force. The Boost and Jump modes pump motionY 0.2 into the column, ten times the liquid force bound, so each hop violates the prediction window and earns a punish with a rubberband; the module's 0.06 ascension value is tuned to stay near the legit window, which is exactly the boundary the check draws. The check also rewards the legitimate exit sequence, so a genuine swimmer surfacing with the vanilla 0.34 or 0.3 exit deltas is not punished.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (faked ground)
countering.explanation: Hawk GroundSpoof compares the client's claimed onGround flag against AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally, a server-side ray trace for solid ground, and punishes the claim when the traced position is not solid unless a client-block placement or a boat explains it. The Boost and Jump modes claim onGround while standing on water, where the server-side trace finds no solid block, so the claim is exposed as a spoof and punished with a rubberband; the Solid and NCP modes do not fake the flag, so they stay out of this check's reach and their exposure remains the envelope checks.
